title: First building option, the calculation modules (one packet, four parts built side by side): A the corner-reach AREA measurement (new, pure, beside lot_reach); B the by-portion coverage arithmetic (ZR 23-362/12-10, from A's two areas); C the two step-P6 buildings as pure functions with their floor schedules; D the preliminary apartment estimate arithmetic. Each part = one new module + one new test; no existing file changes; no part imports another; nothing reachable from a reported result yet [D-090 R147,R192,R239,R255,R256,R322,R509,R519,R540,R541,R543,R545,R650,R688,R700]
objective: Build, as ONE packet with four parts that can be built side by side on different files, the calculation modules the first building option rests on. PART A (the real measurement, new): a pure module beside services/api/app/spatial/lot_reach.py that, from the prepared tax-map outline and the two confirmed straight street lines that meet at the lot's corner, measures the AREA of the part of the outline within a caller-given distance of BOTH street lines (the corner-lot portion) and the area of the rest (the interior-lot portion); measurements only, no legal threshold and no rule named inside, every value a site_geometry SourcedValue or unknown with a plain reason, never a zero or a default. PART B: the by-portion coverage arithmetic - corner portion at 100% plus interior portion at 80% (ZR 23-362; the corner portion is within 100 ft of each street line, ZR 12-10) - taking A's two areas as plain numbers. PART C: both step-P6 buildings as pure functions from plain numbers, each returning its floor schedule and totals; which building an option shows is NOT decided here. PART D: the preliminary apartment estimate arithmetic. No existing file changes; no part imports another part (each takes plain numbers or the existing site-geometry types); nothing any part adds is reachable from a reported result yet; a later wiring step connects them.
business_reason: These are the calculations the first building option needs, in the owner's order after the hand-worked example (D-090 R723). source-075 lets several builders work different parts of the SAME task; one packet means one set of gates and one review over all parts. Building each part as its own small module, checked against the independent step-P6 readings, lets up to three builders work in parallel on different files and lets the arithmetic and the measurement be verified before any result shows a footprint, a building or an estimate.
inputs: The independent reference case docs/reference-cases/R6B/cases/step-p6-worked.json: rows real-lot-coverage-by-portion (corner 9,997.60/9,997.46 at 100%; interior strip 390.39/390.52 at 80%; footprint 10,309.91/10,309.88; outline area 10,387.99 both), made-up-footprint-a (interior lot 10,000 at 80% = 8,000), made-up-building-a/b and real-building-a/b (the storey tables and totals), made-up-estimate-a/b and real-estimate-a/b (the quotients).

The existing model for PART A: services/api/app/spatial/lot_reach.py (M5-T127) and its tests services/api/tests/spatial/test_lot_reach.py (conventions: SourcedValue via site_geometry.labels tax_map_value/unknown_value; PreparedOutline from site_geometry.outline.prepare_outline; SiteGeometry from derive_site_geometry; the benchmark replayed through services/api/tests/spatial/_northern_replay.py replay_lot_geometry + lot_outline_from_mappluto; tolerances quoted to the readings' precision; unknown with a plain reason, never a zero). Read lot_reach.py:1-20 (measurements only, no legal threshold), :51-93 (the dataclasses), :95-174 (street-line + reach helpers), :230-246 (the entry and the all-unknown refusal path).

The law captures docs/research/zr-snapshots/v1/zr-23-362.snapshot.json (interior/through 80%, corner 100%; digest f8370a389af6ffde27b0991b456868be6d9312a67df07e8c5864ea193b40acd9) and zr-12-10-lot-corner.snapshot.json (the corner-lot portion is within 100 ft of each intersecting street line; digest 86b686b683e4ed37531319130ee49dc99a3cba3acbd41c27da2bccb2eb686a58) - the ratios and the 100-ft distance for PART B.

The owner's decided starting assumptions for PARTS C and D: R540 (share 0.60-0.75), R541 (700 sq ft), R542 (10 ft floors), R543 (label), R545 (approval validates nothing), R509 (dividend is the proposed building's floor area, the maximum kept separate), R700 (stay labelled preliminary); the measurement-basis record docs/measurement-basis/MEASUREMENT_BASIS.md (linked, not copied).

Read-only engine context (not changed, not imported): three_way_document.py:97-100,219-223 (the reserved 'not built yet' unit_estimate block); dwelling_units.py:27-58 (the separate legal dwelling-unit limit); building_option.py:1-35 (the existing stacker, neither changed nor imported); result_ways.py:116-119,238-254 (the current building-option and by-portion withholds).
outputs: Per-part reports project-control/reports/M5-T145-part-A.md ... -part-D.md (each builder writes its own); the packet report project-control/reports/M5-T145-producer-report.md is assembled by the orchestrator.
dependencies: No part imports another part. PART B takes PART A's two areas as plain numbers; PART D takes PART C's floor area as a plain number; the links are made by the later wiring step, not inside these modules.
PART A imports only the existing site_geometry package (labels, outline, results) - the same imports lot_reach.py uses; it does NOT import lot_reach itself, the rule engine or the scenario engine.

A later wiring step (outlined in next-pieces-plan.md (c)) hands the site-geometry outline, the two street lines and the 100-ft distance (ZR 12-10) to PART A, feeds A's areas to B, B's footprint to C, and C's floor area to D, then regenerates the committed results document once. Out of scope here.

risks: PART A tolerance for the benchmark lot: the two step-P6 readings differ by at most 0.14 sq ft on the corner portion and 0.13 sq ft on the interior strip, and agree exactly on the outline area (10,387.99). The chosen test tolerance is 1.0 sq ft per portion - about seven times the readings' own spread and ~0.01% of the ~10,388 sq ft lot - and the two parts must sum to the outline area within 0.01 sq ft. This pins no single figure (it requires the program's exact clip within one hand-reader's spread of BOTH readings). I could not run PART A, so the actual program-vs-reading gap is unconfirmed; the builder MUST report the measured gap in part-A.md and, if it exceeds 1.0 sq ft, STOP and surface it as a possible real discrepancy rather than loosen the tolerance silently.

PART A geometry method: shapely==2.0.7 is an admitted, pinned dependency (requirements.txt:508; pyproject.toml:30), so no new package is needed. The RECOMMENDED method, mirroring lot_reach.py's pure-math no-dependency style, is a pure-Python half-plane polygon clip (Sutherland-Hodgman): the corner portion is the outline clipped by {perpendicular distance to street line 1 <= d} and then by {perpendicular distance to street line 2 <= d} (both half-planes are convex, so the clip is exact even for an L-shaped outline); the area is the shoelace of the clipped ring; the interior portion is the outline area minus the corner portion. shapely is an acceptable alternative if the builder prefers; either way no new package.

PART C building A fill rule: storeys = the most full-footprint floors whose running total does not exceed the allowance (made-up A: floor(20,000/8,000)=2; real A: floor(20,150/10,309.91)=1). PART C building B fill rule: the fewest storeys whose top reaches at least the minimum base height (ceil(30/10)=3), spreading the whole allowance over them. Neither building may exceed the maximum base height here (both reach 20 or 30 ft, <= 45), so no setback is worked; the module must not invent a storey above the base.

No part imports another part, and no part changes or imports an existing engine file: PART A imports only site_geometry (not lot_reach); PARTS B/C/D import nothing from each other, from building_option.py, dwelling_units.py, result_ways.py or three_way_document.py. Nothing any part adds is reachable from a reported result in this task.

PART D R387 (no estimator before the measurement basis is resolved) is cleared (see g0_authority): the measurement-basis record (M5-T126) and its decided choices (M5-T135) are accepted, and the owner decided R540/R541.
path_notes:
ONE packet, four independent parts; up to THREE builders. BUILDER SPLIT: Builder 1 takes PART A (the new measurement, the largest and the only geometry); Builder 2 takes PART C (the two buildings); Builder 3 takes PARTS B and D (the two smallest, both pure arithmetic, in two distinct new files). No two builders touch one path: A is in services/api/app/spatial/ + tests/spatial/; B, C and D are four DISTINCT new files under services/api/app/scenario/three_answers/ + tests/scenario/three_answers/ (Builder 2 touches only first_building_options.py + its test; Builder 3 touches lot_coverage_by_portion.py + preliminary_apartment_estimate.py + their tests); each builder writes only its own M5-T145-part-<X>.md. The producer-report.md is assembled by the orchestrator, not a builder.

PART A corner_reach_area.py (pure, measurements only; mirrors lot_reach.py; no legal threshold, no rule named inside).
